rationale: The candidate reads as a coherent early-stage massing with one dominant stepped-courtyard gesture, clear hierarchy, and a legible carved void that can plausibly support neighborhood living. The ground edge is not sealed: the top view shows a substantial internal opening and the four views maintain the same mass rule, so it is not coherent in only one view. The stepped upper profile is more consequential than arbitrary tiering because it wraps an occupiable perimeter around a court rather than behaving like decorative setbacks. The access edge is acknowledged by the void/threshold logic, though the response is somewhat internalized rather than strongly projecting a street-facing seam, so frontage performance is good but not maximal. Program fit is strong because the mass supports mixed-use neighborhood scale, active ground threshold, and upper hierarchy without reading as a tower or large-span hall. Sectionally, the terrace sequence is acceptable and not typologically contradictory, though it could be cleaner as an inhabited roof/terrace edge. Overall it is a solid candidate that aligns with the reference set while remaining distinct.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Three-part low-rise massing with a central void and an upper bridge-like connection creates a legible public center without losing perimeter solidity.

warnings: The access response is legible but slightly inward-looking; a more explicit seam or notch toward the verified frontage could improve street activation.
The silhouette relies on stepped massing; keep it from sliding into repetitive terrace-code rather than one continuous capacity-bearing figure.
